title: Multi-context token-flow calibration for core models
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Goal: Build and maintain a tokens-per-second microbenchmark that captures realistic multi-context workloads (mixed sequence lengths, cache-warmup effects, and concurrent streams) and that feeds regression detection for p95 and throughput.

Scope:
- Develop a canonical "calibration" workload generator that can emit mixed-length requests, grouped user sessions, and KV-cache warmup patterns.
- Implement collectors for raw token rates, per-request latencies, p50/p90/p95/p99, cold vs warm KV cache slices, and sample-level metadata.
- Add statistical regression checks (baseline vs candidate): effect size, KS-test for latency distribution shifts, p95 delta thresholds and false-positive suppression heuristics.
- Integrate harness into CI (nightly and pre-merge smoke) and into the performance dashboard for drift alerts.
- Provide tooling to replay calibration traces against model variants and quantization profiles for root-cause bisects.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness can generate 3 canonical workload profiles (short-chat, long-form, mixed-burst) with configurable token-length distributions
Metrics exporter emits tokens/sec and per-request latencies tagged with cache state (cold/warm) to the metrics pipeline
Automated regression job compares new runs to a stored baseline and raises an alert when p95 increases by >8% with >95% confidence
CI job runs a lightweight calibration on model PRs and blocks merge if throughput regresses beyond defined thresholds
Documentation and runbook describing how to update baselines, add new models, and interpret alerts
